cases.title: A table that styles nothing: the header cell's every default
cases.notes: The floor. If a port disagrees here it disagrees everywhere, and every later row's diff would be noise on top of this one.

cases.title: A table that styles nothing: the first body cell, which is never striped
cases.notes: Striping counts over BODY rows and starts unstriped. Counting over the emitted grid instead shifts every stripe by one when a header is present.

cases.title: The second body row takes the stripe fill
The header fill is the theme accent, not a constant
cases.notes: Every engine hardcoded 8B5CF6 here. That happens to be the DEFAULT accent, so a port that kept the constant passes case 0001 and fails only this one.

cases.title: `borders: false` at table level stops the chain for all four sides
`{all: …, left: false}` keeps three sides and drops one
cases.notes: A port using truthiness rather than key PRESENCE reads `left: false` as absent and leaves the border on.

cases.title: outer/inner: the top-left cell takes outer on left+top, inner on right+bottom
outer/inner: the bottom-right cell is the mirror of 0007
cases.notes: Both corners are pinned because a port that gets `isOuter` from the row only, or the column only, passes one and fails the other.

cases.title: Precedence 1 of 5: a table-level colour reaches a body cell
Precedence 2 of 5: the header band beats the table layer
Precedence 3 of 5: a column's alignment beats the band's
Precedence 4 of 5: the row beats the column
Precedence 5 of 5: the cell beats the row
The highlighted total row: row-level fill, colour and weight together
cases.notes: The construct the whole capability was built for. It is one row-level layer, not a special case anywhere in the engine.

cases.title: Per-side padding overrides only the sides it names
A row drops its bottom rule while the table still asks for one
cases.notes: This is how a KPI figure and its caption become one visual cell. If a port merges border specs instead of REPLACING at each layer, the bottom rule survives and the band grows a line through the middle.

cases.title: Column widths given as weights, summing to the table exactly
Widths <= 1 are fractions; undeclared columns share what is left
cases.notes: The mode boundary is at exactly 1.0, so this row's 0.5 stays in fraction mode while 0017's 2.4 does not.

cases.title: Three equal columns over a total that does not divide by three
cases.notes: 8229601 / 3 rounded independently gives three columns that do not sum to the total. Accumulating and differencing does. The golden is the accumulated answer; if a port matches every other width row and fails this one, that is the bug.

cases.title: A colSpan wider than the table is clamped, not emitted
The covered cell carries `merged` and an empty text, and is not dropped
cases.notes: A row with fewer cells than the grid declares is a corrupt file, not a narrow table.

cases.title: A rowSpan marks the cell beneath it as a vertical continuation
Letter spacing and capitalisation reach a cell run
A nested value an agent meant to DISPLAY is not silently emptied
cases.notes: Object cells used to be JSON-encoded into the text. Reading every object as a cell spec would turn a genuine nested value into a blank cell, so only objects carrying a spec key are treated as one.

cases.title: With no header, grid row 0 is the first DATA row
cases.notes: Every metadataGrid and kpiBand is a header-less table, so this is the common case rather than a corner.

cases.title: A table's fontSize is halved into points, as it is everywhere else in the schema
cases.notes: The halving is a schema-wide convention (fancy-slides designs against a 1920px width), not a table quirk. A port that takes the number as points renders every table at double size and nothing else disagrees.
